title: Largest number in a list
description: find_max(numbers) should return the largest number in a list. The list always contains at least one number, and the numbers can be positive, zero or negative.

bug.summary: maximum starts at 0 instead of a value taken from the list, so a list of only negative numbers returns 0.

hints.1: Think about what your function returns when every number in the list is below zero. Which values can the result ever take?
hints.2: Look at the starting value given to `maximum` on line {line}. Trace the loop by hand with the list [-3, -1, -7].
hints.3: Because `maximum` starts at 0, no negative number is ever larger than it, so the loop never updates it. The starting value needs to be one that comes from the list itself, so that every list gives a fair comparison.
